text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The Privatisation Commission has almost completed the paperwork to start the process of disinvesting 26 percent shares of Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Ltd by June.
- Pakistan will go into next week's crucial talks with India with an open and sincere frame of mind to settle all disputes, a foreign office spokesman said.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said some 5,000 closed industrial units will be revived.
- Sharif has directed the Central Board of Revenue to restructure the tax system so that the common man could pay his tax liability to the government without any fear.
- Watch smuggling causes some 300 million rupees annual losses to the government in the form of customs duties.
- Private rice exporters are likely to export more than one million tonnes of IRRI-6 variety rice and 400,000 tonnes of basmati rice.
- The government has decided to hold the much-delayed housing and population census all over the country.
- Pakistan plans to develop an airborne radar system by next year.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Prime Minister Sharif has taken serious notice of the dearth of wheat flour in different parts of Pakistan.
- The automobile industry has set an export target of $150 million by 2003.

- Corruption, inefficiency, mismanagement, tax evasion and over-staffing are inflicting losses of over 500 billion rupees annually on the national exchequer, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif told legislators.
- Sugar mill owners in Sindh have urged the government to allow exports as over 70 percent of total production was lying in stock, says a worried industrialist.
FINANCIAL POST

- Negotiations between Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) and the cellular phone companies last week have resulted in disagreement over the payment of proceeds to PTCL under the interconnect regime.
THE NEWS
- The government has decided in principle to introduce a low-tax regime, with sales tax likely to be fixed at seven to 10 percent across the board.

- The hiring and firing of political appointees at Pakistan International Airline has begun. The government terminated Capt Aijaz Haroon as general manager Central Control and appointed Capt Humayun Jameel to head the Personnel Department.
- The increase in fuel prices and devaluation of the rupee has burdened Pakistan's two private airlines, Bhoja and Aeroasia with extra spending of over 320 million rupees since July.

- A government committee on the engineering and electronic industries has recommended a growth rate of 25 percent, increasing the share of exports of engineering goods to 20 percent and increasing value addition to 40 percent from 20 percent by the year 2003.
THE NATION
- To align the wobbling economy, a set of far-reaching measures and incentive packages will be announced by the government in a couple of weeks.
- Money changers are shifting $2 million a day to Dubai, causing a setback to government efforts to improve foreign exchange reserves.
THE MUSLIM
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif ordered the Central Board of Revenue to restructure the entire revenue collection system to avoid the huge losses due to tax evasion.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
